Q&A · Speed

Is it fast enough?

CAP alert issuedIMD · CWC · State
SACHETsame feed as SMS
MARK gatewayverify · target · 1.4 KB → 92 B · sign
Inmarsat-6 F1L-band, 84°E
Village receiververify · siren · voice

Target, measured in the pilot: half within 30 s, 95% within 60 s of SACHET issue.

To prove in the pilot: Viasat IoT Nano latency in India, and the BSNL route for alerts.

Delivery is seconds; the bigger delay is often issuing the alert.

So we log sensor-to-issue time on every alert, and SDMAs can pre-authorise sensor alerts.

Q&A · Terrain

Can a deep valley see the satellite?

From Chamoli and Pithoragarh, Inmarsat-6 F1 at 84°E sits ~54° above the horizon, almost due south.

So most villages see it directly — only a narrow gorge or a high ridge right to the south blocks it.

Where a valley can't see it: the antenna goes on a nearby ridge, cabled or radio-linked to the siren.

No dish to aim — the terminal is a small L-band patch.

Elevation angle: our calculation for ~30°N, 79–80°E.

Q&A · Security & false alarms

Can someone fake an alert?

Every frame is signed at the gateway; every receiver checks the signature.

Our prototype already rejects forged, replayed and expired copies.

Gateway runs in two cities for redundancy.

Sirens sound only for the most severe alerts — the rest stay silent to protect trust.

Alerts pass unchanged: the issuing authority stays responsible.

A CAP “cancel” reaches every siren in seconds.

Q&A · Year 3 and beyond

Who keeps it running?

The mitigation fund pays set-up.

A yearly State maintenance contract covers airtime, monitoring, repairs by local Common Service Centre staff, and a custodian stipend.

The State owns the hardware — a lapsed contract is simply re-tendered.

Every receiver reports hourly; silent units are flagged before they're needed.

Lightning guards; installed above the flood line.

Q&A · Regulation

No new law. No spectrum of our own.

1. A sponsor + C-DOT access to SACHET's feed

2. Satellite route — IN-SPACe authorised Inmarsat-6 F1 L-band in India; BSNL's licensed gateway carries Viasat services

3. MTCTE equipment certification

4. SDMF sanction to scale

MARK relays only what authorities issue (DM Act 2005).

The operator holds the spectrum.

No personal data collected (DPDP Act 2023). No towers. Solar power.

Our reading — to be confirmed with the sponsor.

Q&A · Limits

Why not earthquakes?

MARK delivers in tens of seconds. Near an epicentre, shaking arrives faster than that.

So we don't claim earthquake early warning.

Where minutes exist — floods, glacial lake bursts, cyclones, tsunamis, dam releases, landslide alerts — MARK fits.

A tsunami after an earthquake is in scope.
